reason: 'The Khalsa is all of us. Those five are just leading the singing.' The Khalsa is the order of initiated (Amritdhari) Sikhs, not every Sikh, and the five at the head of a Vaisakhi procession represent the Panj Pyare, the first five initiated into the Khalsa (source: Wikipedia, Panj Pyare).

'The Packers were down once, way back when. And look how that turned out.' (pointing at the Super Bowl I clipping) Green Bay never trailed in Super Bowl I; the Chiefs only tied it 7-7 and trailed 14-10 at half (source: Wikipedia, Super Bowl I).

'Emma reached the surf first and swam hard ... She grabbed Theo's arm' A child swimming into a rip current to rescue someone is presented as the right move; NWS/NOAA advice is to get a lifeguard, throw something that floats and yell instructions, since many people drown trying to rescue others (source: weather.gov rip current guidance).

'took ten more shots in the drill, and buried two of them ... Thirteen percent now' One goal on nine shots plus two on ten is 3 for 19, about 16 percent, not 13. (Fact about Ted Williams .406 in 1941 is stated correctly.)

'In Mexico we call it the Mexican wave' (and the Argentine family 'said the same thing'). In Mexico and other Spanish-speaking countries it is called 'la ola'; 'Mexican wave' is the name used by English speakers outside North America (source: Wikipedia, Wave (audience)).

'The problem, he decided, was the order of the colors ... The second one blurred into something smoother, less brown.' The color a fast-spinning disc blends to depends on the proportions of the colors, not the order of the wedges, so rearranging the same colors would not change the blur.

'Nine for Dev, eight for Luca ... Dev's winning sixty percent of the days so far. Luca's at fifty-three.' 9 and 8 wins cannot be 60% and 53% of the same days (that needs 15 days but 17 wins); over the 'thirty-some' days the story mentions they would be roughly 30% and 27%.
'"Nobody answered." Three words.' "Nobody answered" is two words, and the story's lesson is about counting sentence length.

'Spontaneous combustion in the engine, right? That's what makes it go?' Marcus said yes... fuel burning all at once. A model rocket motor is lit by an electric igniter from a launch controller (per Estes/launch-controller guides), not spontaneous combustion, and its propellant burns over a second or two, not all at once. Lee Ross 1977 fact confirmed (Wikipedia, Fundamental attribution error).

'There's a winter league with January tryouts. New year, new cutoff. I'll be the old one for once.' With a January 1 cutoff a December-born player stays the youngest in his birth-year group whenever tryouts are held; the relative age effect depends on birth date relative to the cutoff, not on tryout timing.

'the little generator in the garage ... coughed to life ... the generator humming in the garage.' The CDC says never run a generator inside a home or garage, even with doors open, because of carbon monoxide; the story presents this as normal. Naismith fact is stated correctly.

'Four goals to two, which ... was the equivalent of a two-goal lead the whole second half.' Argentina led the 1930 final 2-1 at halftime and Uruguay scored three second-half goals (sources: goal.com, malaymail World Cup history). The injected fact is stated correctly.

'Six arms. Every single time.' / 'each one of them six-sided'. The fact says snowflakes almost always have six sides; triangular and twelve-sided snow crystals also occur (Libbrecht, Caltech snowcrystals.com).
'He had opened it five times.' The story shows him opening the fridge four times (first, 'again', 'And again', 'the fourth try'). USDA four-hour fact is stated correctly.

'It read minus 12 degrees Celsius... about 10 degrees Fahrenheit, colder than the inside of a freezer.' A home freezer is kept at about -18 C (0 F), so -12 C is warmer than a freezer, not colder (FDA guidance via searshomeservices.com).
The story says wind makes the air feel colder and names the wind chill number, but never gives the mechanism in the fact: wind carries heat away from the skin faster.
The story says there is a middle age with a wide normal range, but never says a large CDC survey found the median age of a first period in the U.S. is about 12.
The story shows one family slurping and concludes 'it wasn't rude here', but never says that in Japan slurping noodles is considered acceptable. Japan is never named.

'"That's not where cartilage is," Ella said' about the elbow, and no one corrects her. The elbow joint has articular cartilage covering the ends of the humerus, radius and ulna (eOrthopod, Elbow Anatomy).
'She bought two baskets and still had coins left for whipped cream.' She had $4.35, and two baskets at $3.50 to $4 each cost $7 to $8, so she could afford only one basket.

'She looked through Maya's lens at the poster: the words shrank. Through her own: the words grew.' This is reversed: Maya's convex (farsighted) lens magnifies and Rebecca's concave (nearsighted) lens makes things look smaller, as the story's own 'your eyes look gigantic and mine will look tiny' shows.
'That old thing is flammable near the curtains.' A space heater is not flammable. The danger is that its heat can set nearby curtains, which are flammable, on fire.

The story explains the online disinhibition effect through Amir ('Psychologists call it the online disinhibition effect') but never mentions John Suler or 2004, which are the specific content of the injected fact.

'Showing him how to hand it over with both hands because one hand was for strangers.' In Chinese etiquette, giving a gift with both hands shows respect (cibtvisas.com and ltl-school.com etiquette guides). There is no rule that one hand is for strangers.

The story never says the paint is acrylic, so its rule that dried paint cannot be washed out is not tied to acrylic. That rule is false for paints like tempera or poster paint, which dissolve in water again. The wet-versus-dry behaviour is shown correctly.

'The crack was on the side that would have been squeezed, and the bend was on the stretched side.' This is reversed: in a greenstick fracture the bone breaks on the stretched (tension, convex) side and bends on the compressed side (Wikipedia 'Greenstick fracture'; AO Surgery Reference).

'The stroller seat reclined all the way back until it lay flat, and it had a hard frame underneath' is presented as meeting the firm, flat safe-sleep rule, with the harness buckled 'loose'. The AAP says strollers and other sitting devices are not recommended for infant sleep; babies should sleep in a crib or bassinet (AAP 2022 guidance), and stroller harnesses should be snug.
'She stood in front of the cooler with five dollars in her pocket' and then pays 'Twelve dollars even' for three $4 bottles. $5 cannot cover $12; the numbers are inconsistent.

After the password is changed, Dad logs in 'using the old password' and gets 'Enter the code sent to your device.' Once a password is changed, the old one is rejected at the first step and no second-factor code is sent.

'It asked for a number, then checked every number from 2 up to the one you entered... She typed 7 and got "prime," also right.' A loop that tests the input itself as a divisor (the bug the story blames for 2) would also report 7 as not prime, so the described debugging trace is wrong.

'a blue logo with a bowl shape... That's the network... Feeding America.' Feeding America's logo is orange and green, not blue (logotyp.us; food-bank brand guidelines: Pantone 144 orange, Pantone 371 green).

'It came from the direction of the pond... the ground sloped downhill toward the water... the slope would make it drift faster and farther.' A wind blowing from the pond pushes the frame away from the pond, uphill, so the slope would slow it, not speed it; the reasoning the plot rewards is backwards.

'She rinsed the chicken, patted it dry' is shown as a normal step in a food-safety story. USDA FSIS advises not washing raw poultry because rinsing splashes bacteria onto the sink and nearby food, including salad.

'If he sneezed on the taco bar on Friday [day five], that would be fine' and the closing 'three days of being a walking sneeze... day five' present people as no longer contagious after day three. CDC (How Flu Spreads) says flu can spread for up to 5-7 days after becoming sick.

'the b had probably once done its job before the vowels moved on without it. It wasn't a guess anymore.' The b in 'subtle' was never pronounced in English; it was added in a Latin-style respelling (from Old French sotil) and has nothing to do with the Great Vowel Shift (Etymonline, 'subtle').
'nine bean plants in paper cups... Three said Fertilizer A, three said Fertilizer B, and one just said Water.' 3 + 3 + 1 = 7, not nine.

'The compound payments did. Three dollars twelve. Three dollars ninety.' At the story's 5% rate ($2.50 on $50), yearly compound interest is $2.50, $2.63, $2.76, $2.89 and $3.04; it never reaches $3.12 or $3.90 within five years.
'eleven, thirteen, twelve, fourteen, ten, twelve, eleven, fifteen, twelve, thirteen... Four of them were twelve.' Only three of the listed answers are twelve (the median is still 12).

Right after saying four-year-olds pass, Priya says 'Little kids just can't believe Sally could be wrong' and that 4½-year-old Marcus 'doesn't know that other people can believe something false', and the demo treats pointing at the fork (where Tyler left the treasure) as the failing answer. In fact, from about age four children pass by saying the character will look where she left it.
The story gives the no-honey-under-12-months rule and says spores can grow in the gut, but never says this causes a serious illness (infant botulism); it only says honey 'could hide trouble'.

'Penelope's number looked bad because she took the most attempts of anyone on the team.' A shooting percentage (makes divided by attempts) is not lowered by taking more attempts, so this 'because' is wrong arithmetic; it also clashes with the story's own claim that her practice percentage beat Roni's.

'Nobody could watch the beaks changing over generations.' Peter and Rosemary Grant did measure it: after the 1977 drought on Daphne Major, the next generation's average beak depth was about 4% larger (source: open.edu OpenLearn / Quanta Magazine coverage of the Grants).

The story never says research on expert performers found this. Targeted practice appears only as Jake's own wondering ('He wondered whether hours of playing a piece mattered less than aiming straight at the weak spot'), not as a finding.
The corn/bean/squash roles are stated correctly, but the story never says the Three Sisters is a method of Indigenous peoples of the Americas; it credits only Mrs. Okafor's grandmother.

The story says the eyes and 'her insides' disagreed, but never names the balance organs in the inner ear or says the brain gets conflicting signals, so the fact's mechanism is not conveyed ('insides' suggests the stomach).

'A front page from June 1871 with a photograph of men in dark coats.' Newspapers could not print photographs in 1871; the first halftone photo in a US newspaper was the New York Daily Graphic's, on 4 March 1880 (source: historyofinformation.com; Wikipedia 'The Daily Graphic').

'I don't think your ears are the problem. I think the background noise is.' (and 'Nobody ever told me it was the noise. They just kept saying I was going deaf.') The fact says hearing loss makes noise hard: trouble following speech in noise is a hallmark and early sign of age-related hearing loss, not proof the ears are fine (source: Wikipedia 'Presbycusis'; hearing-clinic pages).

'On the fourth day, a haze of green threads showed where the carrots slept' (before the beans, on day eight). Carrot seeds are slow, typically 7-21 days to emerge (MSU Extension; Epic Gardening says 14-21), so they would not come up in 4 days or ahead of beans; the bean seed is also not 'about an inch wide'.

'One hand, no weight on the broken side' — the story shows a child with a broken arm in a cast hanging from the monkey bars and frames it as sensible. Children's Wisconsin orthopedic guidance says to avoid monkey bars even for 2 weeks after the cast comes off; hanging one-handed while still in a cast is unsafe.

'a silvery fish with a black stripe... That's a kelp perch... They feed at the edge of things, right where the glass is.' Kelp perch are olive-brown to coppery, not silvery with a black stripe, and feed on small crustaceans among the kelp canopy (palaeo-electronica.org species page; FishBase).

Mom approves replying 'nope' to a prize-scam text as a clever test. The FCC advises 'Do not respond to suspicious texts' (FCC alert, quoted by securityaffairs.com), since replying confirms the number is active; the unsafe practice is presented as fine.

'You're not slower. You were just measured in a different pool.' Long-course (50 m) times are slower than short-course yard times because of fewer turns, so if Priya's summer long-course time was faster than her 25-yard tryout time she really did get slower (source: SwimTopia 'Converting Swim Times', USMS forum).

'Charlie mixed flour and water ... An hour later the dough had risen into a soft, lazy hill.' Flour and water alone do not rise in an hour; bread dough needs yeast or another leavening, which the story never mentions.

'It says best if used by. Not use by.' / calling out 'quality date' or 'safety date'. USDA FSIS says a 'Use-By' date is also a peak-quality date and not a safety date except on infant formula (source: FSIS 'Food Product Dating').

'He measured from the mark [just below his shoulder] down to his wrist bone ... twenty-three centimeters even.' Shoulder-to-wrist length for a child old enough to pitch is roughly 40-50 cm; 23 cm is about the forearm alone (standard segment proportions, judged on knowledge). The arm was also inside a knuckle-to-above-elbow cast, so it could not be measured.

'So near stuff is blurry for me, far stuff is blurry for you,' said by Sadie to farsighted Priya, is the story's last word and is backwards. Farsightedness (Priya) blurs near objects, and Sadie's minifying lenses mean she is nearsighted, so far objects are blurry for her.

The story presents the old building at the nature reserve, signed 'Engine Company 21, 1878', as the famous firehouse ('Engine Company 21, Chicago, 1878. Kid gets it.'). Engine Company 21 was a city firehouse at 313 Third Avenue (later 909 S. Plymouth Court) in downtown Chicago, not a building on a nature reserve (source: Wikipedia, 'Engine Company 21 (Chicago)').
'Him: 10 for 27, which turned into 38 percent.' 10 divided by 27 is 37.0 percent, not 38 percent. Kayla's 5 for 11 = 45 percent is correct.

The story treats holding a fork in the left hand and a spoon in the right as possibly rude at a Malaysian table, and the family approves once Olivia switches to the spoon alone. Fork in the left hand, pushing food onto a spoon in the right, is the standard way Malaysians eat (sources: penang-traveltips.com 'Eat Like A Malaysian'; SBS Cultural Atlas).

'The note with the second and third valves sounded wrong... while the same note fingered with just the first valve came out clean.' Valves 2+3 lower the pitch four semitones and valve 1 two semitones, so they are not the same note in a beginner's range (the usual alternate is 1+2 vs 3); the story also dismisses 'blow different', though lip/air changes are how a trumpet moves between notes (fingering charts, e.g. Wikiversity 'Trumpet').

'She can't take it down... It's saved somewhere else, and that place lets anyone look.' The Internet Archive's help page says site owners can email info@archive.org to have archives of their site excluded from the Wayback Machine.
'Fifty hours was like eighty-five lunches, almost a whole school year of them.' 85 lunches is under half a school year; most US states require about 180 school days (Pew Research, 2023).

'The roast had browned with nothing but its own juices, no sugar anywhere.' The Maillard reaction needs reducing sugars as well as amino acids, and meat contains natural glucose that feeds it; only added sugar was absent (Wikipedia, 'Maillard reaction').

'there it was, a toothpaste study claim from a few years back rated Pants on Fire' by PolitiFact. PolitiFact rates statements by politicians, pundits and viral posts, not product ads (PolitiFact methodology page); the well-known dentist-survey ruling was the UK Advertising Standards Authority's 2007 Colgate decision, and no PolitiFact toothpaste rating was found.
